source_text: μενος· «Ὁ Πατήρ μου μείζων μου ἐστὶ,» καίτοι κατὰ φύσιν θεότητος, ἰσομέτρως ἔχων, καὶ τῆς τοῦ τεκόντος ὑπεροχῆς οὐχ ἡττώμενος. Μῆκος δὲ τῷ ξύλῳ, δεκάπηχυ. Παντέλειος γὰρ ὡς ἐν ὑψώμασι τῆς θεότητος, ὁ Χριστός. Τελειότητος δὲ σημεῖον, ὁ εἰς δέκα τρέχων ἀριθμὸς παρά γε τῇ θείᾳ λαμβάνεται Γραφῇ. Χρυσῆ δὲ τῷ ξύλῳ κεφαλὴ, καὶ μὴν καὶ σῶμα χρυσοῦν. Φύσεώς γε μὴν τῆς ἀνωτάτω καταπλουτεῖ τὸν ἐναυλισμὸν ὁ ἐκ Παρθένου ναός. Σύμβολον δὲ θεότητος, ὁ χρυσὸς, ὑπεροχὴν ἔχων τὴν κατὰ πάντων, ὡς ἐν ὕλης τυχὸν τῆς τοιᾶσδε λόγῳ. Ἐξ ἀργύρου δὲ καὶ ἐκ δυοῖν ἡ βάσις. Λαμπρὸς δὲ καὶ διαφανὴς ἐν γῇ ὁ Χριστὸς, κατά γε τὸ, «Θεὸς Κύριος, καὶ ἐπέφανεν ἡμῖν·» καὶ οἱονεὶ διφυᾶ τὴν γνῶσιν ἔχει· νοεῖται γὰρ ἐν αὐτῷ Θεός τε καὶ ἄνθρωπος. Τουτὶ γὰρ, οἶμαι, ἔστι, τὸ διπλῆν ὥσπερ ἔχειν καὶ ἐξ ἀργύρου τὴν βάσιν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Εἰκάζεις ὀρθῶς. {ΚΥΡ.} Θέα γε μὴν ἐκεῖνο, ὦ τᾶν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὅ τι δή; {ΚΥΡ.} Εἰς αὐλαίας γὰρ δέκα προστεταχὼς ὅλην ἐκτείνεσθαι τὴν σκηνὴν, ἐπιλέγει μεταξύ· «Καὶ ποιήσεις δέῤῥεις τριχίνας, σκέπην ἐπὶ τῆς σκηνῆς· ἕνδεκα ποιήσεις αὐτὰς δέῤῥεις, τὸ μῆκος τῆς δέῤῥεως τῆς μιᾶς ἔσται τριάκοντα πήχεων, καὶ τεσσάρων πήχεων τὸ εὖρος τῆς δέῤῥεως τῆς μιᾶς· τὸ αὐτὸ μῆκος ἐπὶ ταῖς ἕνδεκα δέῤῥεσι. Καὶ συνάψεις τὰς πέντε δέῤῥεις ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ, καὶ τὰς ἓξ δέῤῥεις ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ, καὶ ἐπιδιπλώσεις τὴν δέῤῥιν τὴν ἕκτην κατὰ πρόσωπον τῆς σκηνῆς· καὶ ποιήσεις ἀγκύλας πεντήκοντα ἐπὶ τοῦ χείλους τῆς δέῤῥεως τῆς μιᾶς, τῆς ἀνὰ μέσον κατὰ τὴν συμβολήν. Καὶ πεντήκοντα ἀγκύλας ποιήσεις ἐπὶ τοῦ χείλους τῆς δέῤῥεως τῆς συναπτούσης τῆς δευτέρας.» Τί τὸ χρῆμα λοιπὸν, ὦ Παλλάδιε; δέκα μὲν γὰρ ἐγείρει τὰς αὐλαίας. Εἶτα πῶς οὐκ ἰσάριθμοι ταύταις αἱ δέῤῥεις, περιττεύει δὲ μία, τοῦτ' ἔστιν ἡ ἑνδεκάτη; Συνάψεις γὰρ, φησὶν, τὰς πέντε δέῤῥεις ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ, καὶ τὰς ἓξ δέῤῥεις ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Οὐκ ἔχω φράσαι. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἀλλ' ἥ γε θέσις σαφηνιεῖ τὸ ζητούμενον. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Πῶς ἔφης; {ΚΥΡ.} Πέντε μὲν γὰρ αὐλαίας ἀλλήλαις συνεσφιγμένας ὅτι προσῆκε γενέσθαι φησίν· ἑτέρας δὲ πέντε, κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ δὲ σχῆμα, καὶ ἐν ἴσῳ τρόπῳ ἀντιτεταγμένας. Τοιγαροῦν ἀλλήλαιν καὶ ἀντιπροσώπως ἀντεγηγερμέναιν, ὡς ἐκ βοῤῥέου τυχὸν καὶ νότου, ἤγουν ἐξ ἠοῦς καὶ μέντοι καὶ δυσμῶν, ἑνδεκάτη τις ἡ διὰ μέσου λοιπὸν ἐσχεδιάζετο πλευρὰ, ἀνὰ μέρος ποιουμένη τὰς δέκα, διῃρημένας εἰς δύο, ἐφ' ᾗ τάχα που καὶ δέῤῥις ἡ ἑνδεκάτη περιτετά[ν]νυσται, κρίκοις τε καὶ ἀγκύλαις ἄμφω συνέχοντα τὰς πλευράς· καθ' ὁμοιότητα δὲ τῶν ἄλλων, καὶ οἱ ταύτης στύλοι, πλὴν ἥττους ἐν ἀριθμῷ. Αἱ μὲν γὰρ δέκα αὐλαῖαι, καθάπερ ἤδη προεῖπον, εἰς μῆκος ἐξετείνοντο πήχεων ὀκτὼ καὶ εἴκοσιν, ἥ γε μὴν ἑνδεκάτη καὶ μεσαιτάτη τῶν ἄλλων, τὸ εὖρος τῶν πέντε (τετραπήχεις
pass_a_gloss: [cont.] … ‘My Father is greater (μείζων) than I,’ although according to nature of Godhead (θεότης) holding equal in measure (ἰσομέτρως ἔχων) and not worsted (οὐχ ἡττώμενος) by the superiority (ὑπεροχή) of the one who begot (ὁ τεκών). Length for the wood/post (ξύλον) ten cubits (δεκάπηχυ). For all-perfect (παντέλειος) as in heights (ὑψώματα) of the Godhead is Christ; and sign of perfection (τελειότης) the number running to ten is taken in the divine Scripture. Golden the head (κεφαλή) for the post, and also the body golden. For with the nature most high (ἀνωτάτω) the temple (ναός) from the Virgin (Παρθένος) is enriched (καταπλουτεῖ) as to the indwelling (ἐναυλισμός). Symbol (σύμβολον) of Godhead is gold, having superiority over all, as perhaps in account of such matter (ὕλη). Of silver and of two (ἐκ δυοῖν) the base. Bright (λαμπρός) and clear-shining (διαφανής) on earth is Christ, according to [Ps 117:27 LXX] ‘God is Lord, and he has appeared (ἐπέφανεν) to us’; and as it were of double nature (διφυῆ) he has the knowledge (γνῶσις); for there is understood in him God and man (ἄνθρωπος). This, I think, is the having the base as it were double and of silver. PALL.: You liken rightly (εἰκάζεις ὀρθῶς). CYR.: Look at that, my good man (ὦ τᾶν). PALL.: What then? CYR.: Having ordered (προστεταχώς) the whole tent to be stretched (ἐκτείνεσθαι) into ten curtains, he says in between: [Exod 26:7–10 LXX] ‘And you shall make hair (τρίχιναι) hides/coverings (δέρρεις), a shelter (σκέπη) over the tent; eleven you shall make them; the length of the one covering thirty cubits, four cubits the breadth of the one; the same length for the eleven. And you shall join (συνάψεις) the five coverings together and the six coverings together, and you shall double over (ἐπιδιπλώσεις) the sixth covering at the face (πρόσωπον) of the tent; and you shall make fifty loops on the lip (χεῖλος) of the one covering, the one in the middle at the joining (συμβολή), and fifty loops on the lip of the covering that joins, the second.’ What is the matter then, Palladius? For ten he raises the curtains; then how are the coverings not equal in number to these, but one is over (περιττεύει), that is, the eleventh? For you shall join, he says, the five coverings together, and the six together. PALL.: I cannot say. CYR.: But the placement (θέσις) will make clear (σαφηνιεῖ) what is sought. PALL.: How do you mean? CYR.: For five curtains bound tightly to one another he says must be made, and another five, in the same shape, and in equal manner set opposite (ἀντιτεταγμένας). So, the two having been raised up facing each other (ἀντιπροσώπως ἀντεγηγερμέναιν), as from north and south perhaps, or from dawn and west, an eleventh side through the middle was then contrived (ἐσχεδιάζετο), making the ten apart (ἀνὰ μέρος), divided into two; upon which perhaps the eleventh covering has been stretched around (περιτετάνυσται), with rings (κρίκοι) and loops (ἀγκύλαι) holding together both sides; and like the others its pillars too, but fewer (ἥττους) in number. For the ten curtains, as I already said, stretched in length to twenty-eight cubits, but the eleventh and most middle (μεσαιτάτη) of the others, the breadth of the five (and these four-cubit) … [continues in s.27: is stretched out to about twenty cubits].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …‘My Father is greater than I’ (John 14:28), although in the nature of Godhead he is equal in measure and falls short in nothing of the surpassing greatness of the One who begot him. The length of the post is ten cubits (Exodus 26:16). For Christ is all-perfect, as in the heights of the Godhead, and in the divine Scripture the number that reaches ten is taken as a sign of perfection. The post has a golden capital and a golden shaft as well (Exodus 26:29). Indeed, the temple born of the Virgin is made rich by the indwelling of the highest nature. Gold is a symbol of Godhead, since it ranks above all others, at least as far as such material goes. The base is of silver, and double (Exodus 26:19). Christ is bright and plain to see on earth, according to the saying: ‘God is the Lord, and he has appeared to us’ (Psalm 118:27). And the knowledge of him is, as it were, twofold, for in him are recognized both God and man. This, I think, is the meaning of the base being double, so to speak, and of silver.
Cyril: But look at this, my good friend.

Cyril: He had commanded that the whole tent be spread out in ten curtains, and then he adds in between: ‘And you shall make coverings of hair as a shelter over the tent; you shall make eleven coverings. The length of one covering shall be thirty cubits, and the width of one covering four cubits; the eleven coverings shall have the same length. And you shall join five coverings together, and six coverings together, and you shall fold double the sixth covering at the front of the tent. And you shall make fifty loops on the edge of the one covering, the one in the middle at the joining, and you shall make fifty loops on the edge of the second covering that joins it’ (Exodus 26:7–10). What does this mean, then, Palladius? He sets up ten curtains. How, then, are the coverings not equal to them in number, but one is left over, that is, the eleventh? For he says: ‘You shall join five coverings together, and six coverings together’ (Exodus 26:9).
Cyril: But the arrangement will make clear what we are looking for.

Cyril: He says that five curtains were to be fastened to one another, and another five, of the same form, set opposite in the same way. So when the two sets had been raised facing each other, from north and south, say, or from east and west, an eleventh side was then formed, running through the middle, with the ten on either side of it, divided into two sets. Over it, perhaps, the eleventh covering was stretched, holding both sides together with rings and loops. Its pillars were like those of the others, except fewer in number. anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 9 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens by completing the sentence begun at the end of s.25: Cyril quotes John 14:28 as ‘My Father is greater than me’ (John has ‘the Father’). ‘ἰσομέτρως ἔχων … οὐχ ἡττώμενος’ rendered ‘equal in measure … falls short in nothing’, keeping both negation and the reference to the Father who begot Him. ‘ξύλον’ (the LXX ‘pillar’ or frame of s.25) rendered ‘post’. Ten cubits: Exodus 26:16; gold overlay: Exodus 26:29; two silver bases: Exodus 26:19. ‘ὁ ἐκ Παρθένου ναός’ (Christ’s body as temple) has no single citation. ‘ὡς ἐν ὕλης τυχὸν τῆς τοιᾶσδε λόγῳ’ rendered ‘at least as far as such material goes’. LXX Psalm 117:27 (θεὸς κύριος καὶ ἐπέφανεν ἡμῖν) = English Psalm 118:27; the Hebrew-based English reads differently (‘The Lord is God, and He has given us light’). ‘διφυᾶ τὴν γνῶσιν ἔχει’ rendered ‘the knowledge of Him is twofold … God and man are recognised in Him’; Cyril does not use φύσις here, so ‘two natures’ was avoided. The LXX δέρρεις τρίχιναι (Hebrew ‘curtains of goats’ hair’) rendered ‘coverings of hair’. Exodus 26:7–10 quoted from the LXX; ‘the same length’ follows Cyril’s text (μῆκος). In the last turn Cyril’s reconstruction of the layout is speculative (‘perhaps’), and he uses ‘pillars’ loosely; kept as written. The section ends mid-sentence; the main verb (‘is stretched to about twenty cubits’) falls in s.27.

changes: φύσεώς γε μὴν: 'For' -> 'Indeed' (not a causal particle)
Wrong sense fixed: ἀνὰ μέρος ποιουμένη τὰς δέκα, διῃρημένας εἰς δύο means the middle side has the ten on either side, already divided in two; not that the side 'sets them apart and divides them'
Checked John 14:28, Exodus 26:16, Exodus 26:29, Exodus 26:19, Psalm 118:27 (LXX 117:27), Exodus 26:7–10, Exodus 26:9: all correct
Section ends mid-sentence with '(and these are four cubits each),'; the Greek closing 'δὲ αὖται)' opens s.27, so the s.27 translator should not repeat the parenthesis
